<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{ass:historical-anchor-v2}
The graph \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{H}}\) is connected.
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- assumption-2: body_md -->
\label{ass:calibration-separation-v2}
For each judge \(m\), there exists a constant \(\kappa_{c,m}>0\) such that,
for every \(a_m\in\mathbb R\) and \(\varphi_m\in C(\mathcal X)\),
\begin{equation*}
 \left\|a_m(\theta_I-\theta_J)
       +\varphi_m(\bm{X}_{I}^{m})-\varphi_m(\bm{X}_{J}^{m})\right\|_{C_m}
 \geq \kappa_{c,m}|a_m|.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end assumption-2 -->
<!-- assumption-3: body_md -->
\label{ass:arrival-overlap-v2}
There exists a constant \(\overline w<\infty\) such that, for every \(m\in\mathcal M_A\),
\begin{equation*}
 P_{A_m}^{Z}\ll P_{C_m}^{Z},\qquad
 \frac{dP_{A_m}^{Z}}{dP_{C_m}^{Z}}(\bm{z})
 \leq\overline w
 \quad P_{C_m}^{Z}\text{-a.e. }\bm{z}.
\end{equation*}
Here \(\ll\) denotes absolute continuity.
<!-- end assumption-3 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:historical-arrival-identification-v2}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:historical-anchor-v2},
\ref{ass:calibration-separation-v2}, and \ref{ass:arrival-overlap-v2},
consider two parameter collections
\(\bigl(\bm{\theta},\{c_m,h_m\}_{m=1}^M,\theta_\star\bigr)\) and
\(\bigl(\bar{\bm{\theta}},\{\bar c_m,\bar h_m\}_{m=1}^M,\bar\theta_\star\bigr)\)
that satisfy the comparison models \eqref{eq:human-model-new}, \eqref{eq:hist-surrogate-model-new}, and \eqref{eq:arrival-surrogate-model-new} and the restrictions
\(\bm{\theta},\bar{\bm{\theta}}\in\Theta_0\),
\(c_m,\bar c_m>0\), and \(h_m,\bar h_m\in\mathcal H_m\) for every \(m\).
If they induce the same joint distribution of
\(\bigl(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{H}},\{\mathcal O_{C_m}\}_{m=1}^M,
\mathcal O_A\bigr)\), then
\(\bar{\bm{\theta}}=\bm{\theta}\), \(\bar c_m=c_m\), and
\(\bar h_m(\bm{z})=h_m(\bm{z})\)
\(P_{C_m}^{Z}\)-almost surely for every \(m\), while
\(\bar\theta_\star=\theta_\star\) and
\(\bar h_m(\bm{z})=h_m(\bm{z})\)
\(P_{A_m}^{Z}\)-almost surely for every \(m\in\mathcal M_A\).
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- assumption-4: body_md -->
\label{ass:estimation-geometry-v2}
For each judge \(m\), there exists \(s_m>0\) such that
\(\psi_m^*\) belongs to the H\"older ball
\(C_{d_x}^{s_m}([-1,1]^{d_x};B_\psi)\) defined in
Supplementary Definition~C.1.
<!-- end assumption-4 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:estimation-rates-v2}
Suppose \(K\) and \(M\)
are fixed and
\(n_{\mathrm{H}}\wedge n_\star\wedge\min_{1\leq m\leq M}n_{C_m}\to\infty\).
Suppose also that Assumptions~\ref{ass:historical-anchor-v2},
\ref{ass:calibration-separation-v2}, \ref{ass:arrival-overlap-v2}, and
\ref{ass:estimation-geometry-v2} hold and the two-step estimator uses the
network class in \textup{(C.4)}. Write
\(\Delta\widetilde c_m:=\widetilde c_m-c_m\) and
\(\Delta\widetilde h_{C_m}:=(\widetilde h_m-h_m)(\bm{Z}_{C_m})\). For
\(m\in\mathcal M_A\), also write
\(\Delta\widetilde h_{A_m}:=(\widetilde h_m-h_m)(\bm{Z}_{A_m})\). Then
\begin{align*}
 \|\widetilde{\bm{\theta}}-\bm{\theta}\|_2
 &=O_p(n_{\mathrm{H}}^{-1/2}),
 &
 |\widetilde\theta_\star-\theta_\star|
 &=O_p(n_\star^{-1/2}+r_{\mathrm{Hist}}),\\
 \max_{1\leq m\leq M}\!\left\{|\Delta\widetilde c_m|
 +\|\Delta\widetilde h_{C_m}\|_{C_m}\right\}
 &=O_p(r_{\mathrm{Hist}}),
 &
 \max_{m\in\mathcal M_A}\|\Delta\widetilde h_{A_m}\|_{A_m}
 &=O_p(r_{\mathrm{Hist}}).
\end{align*}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- assumption-5: body_md -->
\label{ass:joint-profile-information-v2}
There is a constant \(\kappa_J>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large
\(n\), \(\bm{b}^\top\bm{\mathcal J}_J\bm{b}\geq\kappa_J\) whenever
\(\|\bm{b}\|_2=1\) and \(\bm{b}^\top\bm{v}_0=0\).
<!-- end assumption-5 -->
<!-- assumption-6: body_md -->
\label{ass:riesz-dnn-approximation-v2}
There is a fixed \(B_\lambda<\infty\) and, for each \(m\), a fixed
\(t_m>d_x/2\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\), there is a
continuous function \(\lambda_{\ell,m}^\circ\) satisfying
\begin{equation*}
 \lambda_{\ell,m}(\bm{x},\bm{x}')
 =\lambda_{\ell,m}^\circ(\bm{x})-\lambda_{\ell,m}^\circ(\bm{x}'),
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\ell,m}^\circ\in C_{d_x}^{t_m}([-1,1]^{d_x};B_\lambda).
\end{equation*}
The equality holds \(P_{C_m}^Z\)-almost surely and, for
\(m\in\mathcal M_A\), \(P_{A_m}^Z\)-almost surely.
<!-- end assumption-6 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:attainment-v2}
Let \(\bm{\ell}\in\mathbb R^{K+M}\setminus\{\bm{0}\}\) be fixed.
Suppose \eqref{eq:inference-sample-size-conditions-v2}, the conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:estimation-rates-v2}, and Assumptions \ref{ass:joint-profile-information-v2}--\ref{ass:riesz-dnn-approximation-v2}
hold, the networks used to estimate \(\lambda_{\ell,m}^{\circ}\) have the
architecture in \textup{(C.6)}, and
\(\Delta_{\ell,n}\to0\).
Then
\begin{equation*}
 v_\ell^{-1}\left\{
 \widehat T_\ell-\bm{\ell}^\top\bm{\beta}
 -\sum_{q\in\mathcal S}\sum_{r=1}^{n_q}
 a_{\ell,q,r}\varepsilon_{q,r}\right\}=o_p(1).
\end{equation*}
Moreover,
\begin{equation*}
 \frac{\widehat T_\ell-\bm{\ell}^\top\bm{\beta}}{v_\ell}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1),
 \qquad \frac{\widehat v_\ell^2}{v_\ell^2}\longrightarrow_p1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat T_\ell-\bm{\ell}^\top\bm{\beta}}{\widehat v_\ell}
 \rightsquigarrow N(0,1).
\end{equation*}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:rank-coverage}
Let \(K\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) be fixed. Suppose the conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:attainment-v2} hold for each contrast loading \(\bm{\ell}_j\),
\(j=1,\ldots,K\). With
\(r_\star:=1+\sum_{j=1}^K1\{\theta_j>\theta_\star\}\), it holds that
\begin{equation*}
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr\{r_\star\in\mathcal C_{\rm rank}\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:human-scale-information-limit-v2}
Let \(\bm{\ell}\in\mathbb R^{K+M}\setminus\{\bm{0}\}\) be fixed.
At a fixed interior point of the parameter space, suppose the conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:attainment-v2} hold.
Then, among regular and asymptotically linear estimators of \(T_\ell\),
the semiparametric efficiency bound satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 V_{\ell,\mathrm{eff}}
 =
 v_\ell^2
 =
 \bm{\ell}^\top\bm{\mathcal J}^{-1}\bm{\ell}>0,
 \qquad
 0\leq V_{\ell,\mathrm{eff}}-B_\ell
 \leq C_\ell/N_J,
\end{equation*}
for some constant \(C_\ell<\infty\).
Moreover, ANCHOR is regular and attains
\(V_{\ell,\mathrm{eff}}\).
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
